blockers.quote: Forty-one messages. Thirty-three dots. And the only one you'd have marked down for spelling is the only one a person typed.
blockers.why: Check #3, Second hook by 0:30: the premise is clear, but the person or relationship you could lose is not identified within thirty seconds.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “Forty-one messages. Thirty-three dots. And one sits on the paragraph from your best friend of eleven years. The wish can tell you who typed it. It can cost you who sent it.”

blockers.quote: You don't send it. Not yet. First you want to know who else.
blockers.why: Check #17, Pull every minute: the listed stake jumps go from about 0:10 to 2:40, leaving roughly two and a half minutes without escalation. This line opens investigation but raises no cost.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “You don't send it. Not yet. First: the dot on your best friend's paragraph. If it survives the one memory only she could know, eleven years changes.”

blockers.quote: Google has offered to suggest your replies since 2015, and to finish your sentences since 2018 (c11).
blockers.why: Check #7, Misconception first: two numbers land in one breath. The same overload recurs in the greeting-card and rooftop facts.
blockers.fix: Replace line 152 with “For years, Google has offered to write your replies and finish your sentences as you type (c11).” Replace line 204 with “For over a century, greeting cards have carried somebody else's printed words under a person's signature (c14).” Replace line 303 with “At its peak, the Philippines sent over a billion texts a day (c02).”

suggestions.quote: You need to see how big it is.
suggestions.fix: Tie the rooftop causally to refusing the offer: “You walk out with the dots still yours. On the roof, you look at what keeping them protects.”

suggestions.quote: Those are the people typing. Everyone else is asleep, or working, or scared of getting it wrong.
suggestions.fix: Avoid claiming one motive for every dark window: “Those are the people typing. The dark windows are messages somebody let a machine carry.”

suggestions.quote: Tomorrow someone will send you three words with a mistake in them. Read them twice. Nobody else could have sent them.
suggestions.fix: Remove the false claim that a typo uniquely identifies its sender: “Tomorrow someone will send you three words with a mistake in them. Read them twice. The mistake may be the part they chose to leave.”

keep.quote: She was keeping you with the only hours she had left: the ones she was asleep for.
Nobody wrote it. Both of you meant it.
